title: Light Speed Stop 4: The Asteroid Belt Lie
topic: Light-speed journey stop 4: the asteroid belt (~10 light-minutes to inner edge at closest; asteroids ~1 million km apart on average; total mass ~3% of the Moon; Ceres ~1/3 of that; salt deposits in Occator crater; Jupiter's gravity prevented a planet)
links_to_previous: Answers episode 3's cliffhanger (is the asteroid belt packed like in the movies?): no, it is almost entirely empty. The journey continues from Mars to the belt, then heads for Jupiter.
hook: The movies lied to you about asteroid belts.
cliffhanger_question: Is Jupiter Earth's protector or its biggest threat?
summary: Answer: no, the belt is almost empty. ~10 light-minutes from Earth to its inner edge at closest, asteroids ~1 million km apart on average, every spacecraft crossed safely. Total mass ~3% of the Moon, about a third of it in dwarf planet Ceres (bright salt deposits). Scientists think Jupiter's gravity stopped a planet forming. Next stop: Jupiter.

scenes.narration: The movies lied to you about asteroid belts.
The answer is no. The belt is almost completely empty.
Light from Earth reaches its inner edge in about ten minutes.
Asteroids there sit about a million kilometers apart, on average.
Stand on one, and you probably couldn't even see the next. Just stars and blackness.
Every spacecraft that crossed it made it through without a collision. No dodging required.
Put all its rocks together, and you get about three percent of our Moon.

visual.query: Moon near side Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter

scenes.narration: And about a third of that is one world, Ceres.
A dwarf planet nearly a thousand kilometers wide, with bright salt in a crater.
So why did this never become a planet? Scientists think Jupiter's gravity stopped it.
Next stop, Jupiter. Is it Earth's protector or its biggest threat? Pick one.
